mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 3-month moving average (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (GDPC1) create a dual-suppression effect on corporate earnings expectations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while GDPC1 decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening with weak demand
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test shows neither PAYEMS nor GDPC1 Granger-causes SPX returns at the 5% level over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 3% in a single month signals excess demand that anticipates future economic expansion, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day SPX forward returns are not statistically different from zero when controlled for the HOUST shock (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102 (2017=100) for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness that reduces market capacity, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 102 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negatively associated with INDPRO contraction (R-squared < 0.01 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% for the first time in three months, the expectation of future monetary easing (as inferred from FEDFUNDS path) tends to push S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for 3 months
regime_hint: labor market tightening toward low-unemployment threshold
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with UNRATE crossing below 4% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer confidence (not available in catalog) would typically signal a strong labor market, but using only PAYEMS, a sharp monthly increase in job openings triggers a short-term risk premium that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: sharp increase in labor market tightness
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are not negatively associated with monthly PAYEMS spikes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggest the Federal Reserve is likely to hold rates steady, which stabilizes discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (HOUST) both show consecutive monthly declines, it indicates dual sector softness that reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases and HOUST decreases in the same month, each for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are not negatively associated with the joint decline in INDPRO and HOUST (p > 0.05 in multivariate regression).
